clue.text: Travel North to Edinburgh, Scotland, seeking work: redden with excitement finding this 24 there

indicators.note: something done with excitement is agitated and thrown about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to head north to the Scottish capital in search of a job, and to blush with eagerness at seeing a famous picture there.
explanation.walkthrough: The 47 letters of TRAVEL NORTH TO EDINBURGH SCOTLAND SEEKING WORK REDDEN, shuffled ('with excitement'), give the title of Raeburn's painting (24 across). It hangs in the Scottish National Gallery in Edinburgh, which is what 'there' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The skating minister is the best-known portrait by the Scottish painter Henry Raeburn, so it is the picture by that artist to be found in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Cross-border article missing from Scottish port about unknown queen's jesters

parts.note: a cross can be T-shaped, so it gives T
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

indicators.note: about means going round, so the port's letters surround the unknown
an article that is missing from a word has been taken out of it

parts.note: Arbroath is a fishing port on the east coast of Scotland
A is the indefinite article
X is the algebraic unknown
ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth, here with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Some cross-border item has gone astray from a Scottish harbour, apparently connected with an unidentified queen's court fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-border' reads as one adjective but splits into two pieces. Arbroath less its A ('missing from') goes 'about' the unknown, and ER is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The film comedians Groucho, Chico, Harpo and Zeppo were clowns of the screen, so jesters is a playful description.

clue.text: Genuine heart afflicted by languor

indicators.note: afflicted means troubled or upset, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
the heart of a word is its middle, here all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sincere heart is troubled by listlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes ENUIN from GENUINE, and 'afflicted' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weary boredom, a listless lack of energy, which is what languor means.

clue.text: Pastoral defect in some clergy heading off villain

indicators.note: a defect is a falling short, so only a fragment lying within the words some clergy is used
with its heading off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A rural flaw is found among certain clergymen, while a rascal is being headed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defect in' takes ECL from the middle of 'somE CLergy'; 'heading off' removes the first letter of ROGUE to leave OGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, such as Virgil's dialogues between shepherds.

clue.text: Message to home number, first to last, is no longer with us

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the last position, so the opening letter goes to the end

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
in means at home
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

explanation.surface: A text sent to a home phone number reports that someone has died.
explanation.walkthrough: TEXT + IN + C makes TEXTINC; 'first to last' sends its opening T to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely no longer exists, which is the sense of the phrase in the clue.

clue.text: Ready for school with due reform being on message

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire

explanation.surface: A pupil is fit to start lessons, having duly reformed and toed the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges the three letters of 'due'; 'being on' places them before the telegram. 'On message' looks like political loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educable is capable of being taught, and so fit to be sent to school.

clue.text: See 1 across
"Facilis descensus Averno" — keeping count?

indicators.note: a word keeping something holds it within itself, so the answer sits inside the Latin word

explanation.surface: Virgil's line that the descent to Hell is easy is quoted, with a question about keeping a tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' says the Latin word holds the answer: desCENSUS. Virgil's tag means 'the descent to Avernus (the underworld) is easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population.

clue.text: Description of Abraham going to press?

parts.note: Abraham came from Ur of the Chaldees, so he could be described as a man of that city
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A question about the right way to describe the biblical patriarch heading off to the newspaper printers.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham was a 'gent' from Ur, so he is an UR GENT. 'Going to press' looks like newspaper printing, but here it means pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something urgent presses for attention, so it is described as pressing, which the clue's phrase hints at playfully.

clue.text: English sailors clad in duck never changing

indicators.note: sailors clad in duck are wrapped in it, so the duck's letters go round them

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: English seamen dressed in duck, the hard-wearing cloth, look the same as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the canvas cloth sailors wore, but it is the bird; 'clad in' wraps it round the sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever and so never alters.

clue.text: Heavenly sound puts theology in lower place

parts.note: TH is an abbreviation for theology
under means in a lower place, beneath

explanation.surface: A church sermon that drops theology to a humbler position.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is the noise from the skies that follows lightning, a sound from the heavens.

clue.text: See 1
Leave bed — it means more money

definitions.meaning: to get up in the morning

explanation.definitionFit: To get up from bed is to rise; a rise in pay is an increase in salary.

clue.text: Sound of instrument suitable for the blues?

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is said, so the answer is said like the instrument

parts.note: the sax is short for saxophone, a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A saxophone's tone suits a blues band.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'blues' look musical, as the sax is a blues instrument, but they are colours: saxe is a light greyish blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxe blue is a shade of blue, so the word fits among the blues in a crossword's playful sense.

clue.text: First time up — see if the stairs are OK?

definitions.meaning: an aircraft's maiden trial in the air

definitions.text: see if the stairs are OK?
definitions.meaning: jokingly, a trial run up a staircase, or set of steps

explanation.definitionFit: A new aircraft's trial flight is its first time airborne; stairs come in flights, so checking them is jokingly a trial of a flight.

clue.text: Platonic nexus scattered — turn first left

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a U-turn gives U
A means first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A connection is broken up, and someone is told to take the first left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges 'nexus'; 'turn first left' looks like a driving direction but gives three single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Platonic relationship is affectionate but not sexual.

clue.text: Gunners surround African country unable to wait, as they say

definitions.text: unable to wait, as they say

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
a ring is something that surrounds
Togo is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Artillery forces encircle a West African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surround' looks like a verb, telling the Gunners to encircle the country, but it is a noun giving RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring to go is an idiom for being eager to start, unable to hold back.

clue.text: See 1 across
Old comedian demolishing Centrepoint?

indicators.note: a building being demolished is broken down, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: An elderly comic is knocking down a London tower block.
explanation.walkthrough: Centrepoint is a London office tower; split it into CENTRE and 'point' (E), and 'demolishing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman playwright of comedies, so an ancient writer of comic drama.

clue.text: Profitable employment is just as well

definitions.meaning: a phrase of relief that things turned out fortunately

explanation.definitionFit: A well-paid post is a fine piece of work to have, and the phrase also says something turned out fortunately.

clue.text: Anxiety for the return of liberal Tories?

indicators.note: the return of a word turns it back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: wets was the name given to moderate Conservatives who opposed Margaret Thatcher's policies

explanation.surface: Worry about the comeback of moderate Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1980s Britain, the 'wets' were the moderate Conservatives (Tories) in Thatcher's cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be anxious and agitated, so stew means a state of worry.

clue.text: See 1 across
Flier with explosive dip

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: A bird or aircraft carrying explosives makes a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to take a swim or quick dip in water.

clue.text: Passageway ahead: Reagan not having died, enter turncoat

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the second piece goes inside the first
a name not having a letter has it removed

parts.note: Ronald was President Reagan's first name

indicators.note: a turn is a change of order, so the letters of coat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ahead lies a passage where Reagan, still alive, admits a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turncoat' looks like a traitor, but it splits: 'turn' rearranges 'coat', which goes inside the president's first name minus D for died ('enter', 'not having').
explanation.definitionFit: A root canal is the channel through a tooth's root, a passage in the head.

clue.text: What Burns's mouse did to homecoming beast? Not sure

parts.note: cows come home, as in the saying 'till the cows come home'
er is the sound of hesitation of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Robert Burns's mouse behaved somehow towards a beast returning home, the speaker is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns's poem To a Mouse addresses a 'wee, sleekit, cow'rin, tim'rous beastie'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouse in Burns's poem was 'cow'rin', so it was shrinking in fear, and cower means to crouch in fear.

clue.text: Sir Henry gets audience back on-stream

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: an ear is an audience, a hearing, as in 'lend an ear'
burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A knight finds a hearing again now that he is producing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the reversed ('back') audience before the stream; 'on-stream' looks like the business phrase for production starting. A burn is a Scottish stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Raeburn was the Scottish portrait painter, knighted in 1822.

clue.text: Max gets worse, they say, rendering Samson's weapon

annotationWithheld.why: Max gets worse, they say, rendering Samson's weapon (7): JAWBONE fits 'Samson's weapon', but no homophone of 'Max gets worse' giving JAWBONE could be found
annotationWithheld.clue: Max gets worse, they say, rendering Samson's weapon

clue.text: Argentine peeler has medal to flog

parts.note: silver is the medal for second place
to birch is to flog with a birch rod

explanation.surface: A policeman from Argentina has a medal to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine peeler' looks like a policeman from Argentina (peelers were early British police), but argent means silver: it is the silvery tree whose bark peels.
explanation.definitionFit: The silver birch is a tree with silvery-white bark that peels off in strips.
